lesson_title: The Tuckshop Truth: One Subtraction Decides Everything
hook_text: Her cash tin held R2 640. Her actual profit? R690. Here's where the money went.
clip_script: Three words carry the whole topic. Income is money flowing in. Expenditure is money flowing out. Profit is what remains when expenditure is subtracted from income. Zanele's tuckshop month: 190 vetkoek at R6 is R1 140, plus 150 cans at R10 is R1 500 — R2 640 in. Now the out side: R1 400 of stock, R250 rent, R180 gas, R120 taxi — R1 950 out. The profit line: 2 640 minus 1 950 equals R690. And watch the ten vetkoek she made but never sold — their ingredients cost R25, spent whether or not anyone buys. Unsold stock quietly eats profit.
visual_style: Animated cash tin filling with green coins, then bills flying out one by one with labels, ending on a glowing R690 — and ten sad vetkoek fading to grey with -R25 above them.
pacing: Quick money-in montage, itemised money-out beats, slow reveal of the profit line and the unsold-stock sting.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to build the statement that settles every money argument.
